title: Decompose routing state machine; remove legacy coordination & upgrade async deps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: the smart-router has accumulated a large implicit state machine implemented across multiple modules (policy-evaluator, capacity-checker, fallback-queue, decision-committer). This makes it hard to enforce invariants, reason about edge cases during partial failures, and blocks a planned upgrade of our async runtime and metrics client. Goal: introduce an explicit, composable routing state machine API that splits the path into clear stages, removes legacy global coordination locks, and enables an in-place upgrade of async dependencies (tokio/generic executor and our internal metrics client).
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a documented RoutingStateMachine interface with stages: EvaluatePolicies -> CheckCapacity -> EnqueueFallbacks -> CommitDecision
Remove at least 85% of usages of the legacy global coordination mutex (router.lock) on the hot path
Upgrade async runtime dependency to tokio v1.12 and internal metrics client to metrics-client v2.0 without functional regressions
E2E latency regression <= 3% p50 and p95 compared to baseline for 90th percentile sequence lengths
New state transitions are covered by unit tests and a small integration harness that simulates region failovers
Rollout plan executed: canary on staging, gradual ramp to 25% production traffic with automatic rollback on error-rate spike
notes: Decision: favor composability over a single monolithic refactor — implement a state machine facade that can orchestrate existing modules rather than rewrite all internals in one PR.
Trade-offs: incremental approach increases short-term surface area (adapter shims) but reduces risk and allows parallel work on async upgrades.
Key risk: subtle ordering regressions when moving fallback enqueue earlier — added integration tests to cover partial failures during KV cache misses.
We will keep the old policy evaluator adapter in place until deprecation milestone; feature flag guards the new state machine path.

work_log: 2026-02-25: Ticket created by Aisha to capture decomposed state machine and async upgrade work
2026-03-01: Spike complete — validated that policy-evaluator and capacity-checker can be expressed as pure 'stage' handlers (notes in design doc)
2026-03-04: Prototype facade implemented (PR #3782) and gated behind feature flag 'new_routing_sm'
2026-03-06: Discovered a path where fallback enqueue before commit causes double-counting of inflight tokens when KV miss + retry occurs — added invariant check and test case
2026-03-09: Integrated metrics-client v2 in a branch; observed 4% p95 regressions due to synchronous metric flush on hot path, fixed by batching in pr #214

2026-03-11: Canary deploy to staging with 5% traffic for 24h, observed minor increases in tail latency for very short sequences (p99 +6%). Investigation points to lock removal and new task scheduling; optimizing executor usage next.
2026-03-12: PagerDuty incident test passed with new fallback ordering — fallback enqueues now idempotent under duplicate retries
test_plan: Unit tests for each stage handler and transition table; integration harness that runs synthetic traffic across region failover scenarios (script: tests/harness/routing_state_sm_harness.sh); A/B compare latency and error rates against stable for 48h; run chaos tests that drop region connection mid-flow to validate rollback and fallback behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind 'new_routing_sm' feature flag. 2) Canary: 1% prod traffic for 2h; monitor errors, latency, drop in throughput. 3) Ramp to 5% for 24h. 4) Ramp to 25% for 48h with automatic rollback on error-rate > 0.5% or latency regressions >5% p95. 5) Full rollout if metrics stable. Post-rollout retrospective and remove legacy lock uses in a follow-up sprint.
testing_notes: Observed race in PR #3782 when policy evaluator returns 'defer' and capacity-check resolves concurrently; added an explicit 'defer' to 'enqueue fallback' mapping and a test that simulates concurrent worker threads.
Added end-to-end observability hooks: emitted 'routing_stage_enter' and 'routing_stage_exit' traces for easier postmortem and latency attribution.
